# Phasing polyploid gene copies with homologizer

[homologizer](https://github.com/wf8/homologizer) (Freyman et al.) runs in RevBayes:
it jointly infers one tree and the assignment of each polyploid gene copy to a subgenome (mul-tree tip).
Scripts live in `scripts/homologizer/`. Run everything from the project root.

## 1. Pull OTU alignments from Hyak

```{bash}
./scripts/homologizer/sync_hyak.sh pull
```

Pulls `output/june3/purc_pool{A,B}/<LOCUS>/<LOCUS>_recluster/<LOCUS>_OTUs.aligned.fa`
(and the non-reclustered `<LOCUS>_OTUs.aligned.fa`, used as a fallback, e.g. GAPCPSH)
into `output/homologizer/raw/`. Change `RUN_NAME` in the script for a different run.

## 2. Pick taxa, realign

```{bash}
julia --project=. scripts/homologizer/prep_homologizer.jl
```

The first run writes `input/homologizer/taxa.csv` from the sampling sheet:

- `include`: pre-set to `yes` for pools A/B with ploidy 2/3/4. Trim this, because runtime scales with the number of tips.
- `n_copies`: subgenomes (mul-tree tips) per sample: diploid 1, tetraploid 2, triploid 3.

Rerun the script after editing. For every locus it:

1. keeps the top `n_copies` OTUs by read size (size >= `MIN_SIZE`, default 10) per sample;
   plastid loci keep only the top OTU
2. names diploids `<purc_id>` and polyploid copies `<code>_copy1..k`
3. realigns pools A + B together with MAFFT and writes `output/homologizer/aln/<LOCUS>.fa`
   (aligned FASTA; RevBayes reads it directly, no NEXUS conversion needed)
4. writes the Rev snippets in `output/homologizer/rev/` (initial phase, phasing moves)

Check `output/homologizer/copy_summary.csv` to see which OTU each copy name is per locus.

Notes on the model:

- Missing polyploid copies become `<code>_BLANK<n>` (all `?`), so the phaser can still put them on a tip.
- Plastid loci get no phasing moves. Their single copy stays fixed on tip `_A`, so **tip A = maternal subgenome**.
- All loci (including plastid) share one tree, the standard homologizer assumption.

## 3. Run locally

```{bash}
conda create -n revbayes -c conda-forge -c bioconda revbayes
conda activate revbayes
mkdir -p log
nohup ./scripts/homologizer/run_homologizer.sh 2 > log/homologizer.out 2>&1 &
```

The `conda create` line only needs to run once.
This runs 2 independent replicates in parallel (run id = seed) to `output/homologizer/mcmc/run<N>.*`,
with each run's screen output in `log/homologizer_run<N>.out`. Pass a different number for more replicates;
each one uses a single core. `nohup` keeps the runs going if the terminal closes.
Generations and sample frequency are set at the top of `homologizer.Rev`.
Test run (146 samples / 182 tips / 9 loci): about 0.6 s per generation.

### Test run on a small subset

To check the pipeline before the full run, trim `taxa.csv` to 18 samples (23 tips):
the 2 diploids with the most OTUs per species, 3 tetraploids (including the viscosa × triangularis hybrid KMW043), and 1 triploid.
The full template is backed up to `taxa_full.csv` first.

```{bash}
cp input/homologizer/taxa.csv input/homologizer/taxa_full.csv
TEST="KMW147 KMW023 KMW078 ES315 KMW008 KMW166 KMW134 KMW049 KMW188 KMW143 ES288 KMW148 ES304 ES281 KMW129 KMW122 KMW043 KMW191"
awk -F, -v OFS=, -v t="$TEST" 'BEGIN{n=split(t,a," "); for(i=1;i<=n;i++) k[a[i]]=1}
NR==1{print; next} {split($1,p,"_"); $5 = (p[1] in k) ? "yes" : "no"; print}' \
  input/homologizer/taxa_full.csv > input/homologizer/taxa.csv

julia --project=. scripts/homologizer/prep_homologizer.jl
conda activate revbayes
./scripts/homologizer/run_homologizer.sh 1 200
nohup ./scripts/homologizer/run_homologizer.sh 2 > log/homologizer.out 2>&1 &
```

The first `run_homologizer.sh` call is a smoke test (1 run, 200 generations, a few seconds);
the second is the real test (2 runs, 50,000 generations, about 15 min).
The second argument to `run_homologizer.sh` overrides `n_gen`. The subset runs at about 0.015 s per generation.
To go back to the full sample set, restore the template and rerun the prep script:

```{bash}
cp input/homologizer/taxa_full.csv input/homologizer/taxa.csv
```

## 4. Results

Output is in `output/homologizer/mcmc/`:

- `run<N>.log`: check convergence in Tracer, and compare the two runs
- `run<N>_<LOCUS>_phase.log`: copy assigned to each tip per sample. Summarize with burn-in removed.
- `run<N>_map.tree`: unrooted, so root it before plotting.
  Plot phasing with homologizer's `src/plot_phase.R`.

To test homeologs vs alleles for a sample (e.g. 2 vs 3 tips), set `bayes_factors = TRUE`
and compare stepping-stone marginal likelihoods between `taxa.csv` versions.
